title: Measuring Definition Sensitivity in LLM Annotation of Social Science Concepts
abstract: arXiv:2611.13339v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In social science research, text annotation is a fundamental task that is traditionally a costly, hard-to-scale manual process. Researchers have used large language models (LLMs) to perform annotation by writing a definition of a concept into a prompt - a rule that determines whether a label should be attributed to a text depending on its content. However, concepts such as hate speech, fake news, and terrorism typically have several theoretically defensible competing definitions. It is also unknown whether the model actually applied the definition to provide the label or the label was based on the model's pretrained notion of the concept. To test this, we have the model annotate the same texts twice, each time with a different definition. We call the disagreement between the two sets of annotations definition sensitivity. translated_title: 测量大语言模型在社会科学概念标注中的定义敏感性
translated_abstract: 在社会科学研究中，文本标注是一项基础性任务，传统上是一个成本高昂、难以规模化的人工过程。研究人员已开始使用大语言模型（LLM）进行标注，方法是将概念的定义写入提示词中——这是一条根据文本内容决定是否为文本赋予相应标签的规则。然而，仇恨言论、假新闻和恐怖主义等概念通常存在多个在理论上均可成立、相互竞争的定义。此外，目前尚不清楚模型究竟是真正应用了所给定义来产生标签，还是标签基于模型预训练中对概念的固有认知。为检验这一点，我们让模型使用不同的定义对相同文本进行两次标注，并将两组标注之间的分歧称为“定义敏感性”。作为对照，我们对其中一个定义进行改写但保持其要求不变——两组标注之间的分歧……
tldr: 该论文提出“定义敏感性”这一新指标：让LLM使用不同定义对同一批文本分别进行标注，通过两组标注结果的分歧程度来衡量模型是否真正遵循了给定定义，还是仅仅依赖其预训练中形成的固有概念认知。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces "definition sensitivity"—measuring the disagreement between LLM annotations of the same texts under different definitions—to test whether the model genuinely applies the given definition or merely relies on its pretrained notion of the concept.
